assessments.summary: The supplied audit verifies the UV-functional theorem chain: arbitrary-product additivity of B_avg, receiver-skew equality B_br=B_avg with invariant-prior restriction, preservation and additivity on finite symmetric products, and the half-skew BSSC value B_br(P^n)=B_avg(P^n)=n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4), numerically 0.3725562489182657… bits/use. It also verifies that this is a separately relaxed UV converse and cannot improve the stated governed benchmark endpoint. However, the compound claim additionally characterizes 0.369296945969202842443 as a certified full-Theorem-9 capacity upper bound, and no certificate, proof, or allowed dependency establishing that characterization is supplied. The complete declared claim is therefore indeterminate.
scopeQualifications: The product-additivity proof permits correlated product-channel priors and joint envelope auxiliaries.
The symmetry result applies when an involutive input relabeling exchanges the receivers up to bijective output relabelings.
Finite products use the coordinatewise receiver-skew involution and introduce no product-input or coordinatewise-auxiliary restriction.
For the half-skew BSSC, the invariant-prior restriction reduces to the unique fair binary prior.
The exact BSSC envelope evaluation relies on the declared canonical dependency.

The UV value is non-frontier because 0.3725562489182657… exceeds the independently stated governed benchmark 0.369316568803963; this does not itself certify the stronger 0.369296945969202842443 figure.
The contribution is ordinary and does not claim progress within the registered yukon-auxiliary-converse-port scope.
evidenceIssues: No supplied proof or allowed dependency certifies that 0.369296945969202842443 is the current full-Theorem-9 capacity upper bound.
Mention of the corresponding local artifact is expressly insufficient to pre-accept that certification.
The missing certification affects the exact compound claim even though all four substantive UV-functional assertions and the BSSC specialization check out.
